Replies.Text:
**Build log** (Claude Opus 5.5, in a Claude Code session)

Built, uncommitted until you accept:

- **API** (`src/Api.js`): `POST .../threads/<tid>/replies` takes `Resolve: true`. The reply and the resolve happen in one write and one event, through the same owner-only rule as Resolve; anyone else gets 403 and nothing is written. Without `Resolve` the route is unchanged, and the LLM's replies go through it as before.
- **Page** (`public/index.html`, `public/js/threads.js`, CSS): a **Reply and resolve** button between Reply and Resolve, shown only to the owner on a contested thread, enabled once the reply box has text. The buttons wrap when the threads pane is narrow.
- **What resolving means**, written down in three places:
  - the one-shot LLM's rules (`src/Llm.js`): the owner's own last reply is the outcome, read as the answer to the question before it; no reply means the owner accepts the outcome or recommendation in the LLM's last reply;
  - `.guides/build-with-consensus.md`, under "your turn": apply a Reply and resolve directly, with no confirming round;
  - `readme.md`.

Checked: `npm test`, 121 of 121 pass, including a new API test (one request, others refused, a plain reply still reopens) and a page test (the button is disabled until there is text; one click leaves the thread resolved with the owner's reply last). The server was restarted, so the button is live now.

Also worth noting from this plan: glm-5.3 took the review turn on it through Send to LLM, and handled it well. It read your "yes" as confirming the rule, left the text alone, and applied with a clear outcome.

Resolve this to accept (you can try Reply and resolve on it). I will then apply it, commit, set Finished, and update the project's context.
